d.d: To even the slightest extent; at all.
Used before different, before comparatives with more and less, and idiomatically before other comparatives, generally in interrogative, hypothetical, or negative contexts.
d.x: If you get any taller, you'll start having to duck through doorways!

d.d: Used to modify a verb, generally a finite verb or a non-finite verb in object position.
d.x: That doesn't bother me any.

d.d: One at all; at least one; at least one kind of; some; a positive quantity of.
d.x: Do you have any biscuits?

d.d: A/an, each or some, no matter its/their identity or nature.
d.x: Choose any item you want.

d.d: An unspecified but imminent (second, minute, day etc.).
d.x: They'll be arriving any day.

d.d: Any thing(s) or person(s).
d.x: Any may apply.

d.d: Any one out of an indefinite number of persons; anyone; any person.
d.x: Anybody will do.

d.d: A person of some consideration or standing.
d.x: Everybody who wants to be anybody will come to Jake's party.

d.d: In any way or manner whatever.
In any case. Used to indicate that a statement explains or supports a previous statement.
d.x: Anyhow, he is dead now.

d.d: Without care or tidiness; recklessly, negligently or randomly.
Random, careless, offhand, disorderly; done without thought or consideration.
Alternative form of any more.
d.x: He doesn't live here anymore.

d.d: Any person; anybody.
d.x: Almost anyone can change a light bulb.

d.d: At a non-specific place; anywhere.
Any object, act, state, event, or fact whatsoever; a thing of any kind; something or other.
d.x: I would not do it for anything.

d.d: Expressing an indefinite comparison.
Someone or something of importance.
Used as a placeholder verb for any verb out of a set of related verbs.
d.x: He wasn't cooking, he wasn't sweeping, he wasn't anythinging!

d.d: In any way, any extent or any degree.
d.x: That isn't anything like a car.

d.d: At any time.
d.x: I don’t like beer much. Give me a fine wine anytime.

d.d: A form of you're welcome in response to thank you or thanks.
d.x: Thanks so much for looking after grandpa. ~ That’s all right. Any time, dawg.

d.d: suitable for any time; not associated with any particular time.
Regardless; anyhow.
d.x: He didn't enjoy washing his car, but it was so dirty that he did it anyway.

d.d: Used to indicate that a statement explains or supports a previous statement. See anyhow and at least.
d.x: I don't think that's true. I haven't found any evidence, anyway.

d.d: Used to indicate a change of subject.
Anyway, anyhow, in any case.
In or at any location.
d.x: I don't know where I left my keys. They could be anywhere.

d.d: To (in the direction of) any location.
d.x: Anywhere you go in France, there will be bread and wine with dinner.

d.d: Any location or an unknown location.
d.x: Anywhere is better than here!

d.d: A person without strong cultural or social ties that are exclusive to a specific place.
Alternative spelling of anyhoo.
